surface_summary: John Ashton, a wealthy man recently settled in London, is found murdered in a narrow passage. Langton Hyde, an impoverished actor, is arrested for the crime after being seen fleeing the scene with one of Ashton's rings. However, a complex investigation reveals a secret involving the Ellingham title and estates, leading to the uncovering of imposture and conspiracy.
accepted_facts: John Ashton was murdered in Lonsdale Passage, stabbed through the heart.
Langton Hyde was seen fleeing the scene and found with one of Ashton's rings.
Ashton possessed secret papers relating to the Ellingham title and estates.
Miss Wickham is Ashton's ward and heir to his fortune.
inferred_conclusions: Langton Hyde was the murderer motivated by robbery.
The murder was a simple robbery gone wrong.
Mrs. Killenhall and Dr. Cortelyon were innocent parties.
mechanism_description: Dr. Cortelyon, motivated by greed for the secret papers and wealth, murdered John Ashton by stabbing him in the back in a narrow passage. Mrs. Killenhall acted as his accomplice, assisting in the conspiracy and attempting to defraud Miss Wickham. They planted evidence to implicate Langton Hyde, who was innocent and unwittingly involved.
delivery_path: Dr. Cortelyon awaited Ashton in the passage, knowing his habits.
He stabbed Ashton swiftly with a keen-edged weapon through the heart.
The body was placed in the passage to be discovered.
Mrs. Killenhall and Cortelyon removed important papers and valuables.
They planted some papers and valuables with Langton Hyde to frame him.
Hyde found the ring and fled, unaware of the murder details.
The conspirators attempted to manipulate the inheritance and cover their tracks.
outcome_result: Dr. Cortelyon and Mrs. Killenhall are arrested and charged with the murder of John Ashton, clearing Langton Hyde and restoring Miss Wickham's rightful inheritance.

false_assumption.statement: Langton Hyde was the murderer who killed Ashton for robbery.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: Hyde was seen fleeing the scene with one of the victim's rings and was found in possession of a knife matching the murder weapon. The circumstantial evidence strongly pointed to him.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the involvement of the real murderer, Dr. Cortelyon, and the conspiracy to frame Hyde, as well as the true motive related to secret papers and inheritance.

supporting_points: Seen running away from the murder scene
Found with one of Ashton's diamond rings
Possessed a knife similar to the murder weapon
Confessed to picking up the ring near the body
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Hyde had no motive to kill and was starving, making it unlikely he committed the murder; planted evidence was used to implicate him.

red_herrings.description: Hyde's attempt to pawn a diamond ring taken from the victim was used as evidence of guilt.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Hyde was starving and desperate, unaware of the ring's true value and innocence of the murder.

red_herrings.description: A man claiming to be the missing Lord Marketstoke appeared with documents stolen from Ashton, confusing the inheritance issue.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The claimant was a cat's-paw used by the real murderer to mislead the investigation.

closed_circle.rationale: The suspects were limited to those with access to Ashton and motive related to the secret papers and inheritance; others were excluded by alibis or lack of opportunity.

discriminating_test.design: The claimant was brought before solicitors who knew the real Lord Marketstoke and the missing finger detail. They observed the claimant's hand to see if the middle finger was missing and examined his knowledge of family history and documents. The test revealed the claimant's recent finger amputation inconsistent with the historical injury, exposing him as an impostor.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The claimant's physical and documentary evidence did not match the real Lord Marketstoke, proving he was a fraud used by the real murderer to mislead the investigation.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The claimant must have the middle finger of his right hand missing with a recent scar; failure to meet this condition exposes imposture.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given detailed descriptions of characters, their movements, and the evidence found, including the defective typewriter letter, the missing finger detail, and the suspicious behavior of Mrs. Killenhall and Dr. Cortelyon. Clues such as the chemical-smelling papers and the planted valuables are presented openly. The involvement of the claimant as a cat's-paw is hinted through inconsistencies and the legal scrutiny. The reader could have solved the case by piecing together these clues and questioning the motives behind the planted evidence.
